12264. **Error-oracle deserialization check** — distinguishes deserialization errors from generic bad-input errors through class-specific tokens.
12265. **Timing-oracle deserialization proof** — uses gadget-triggered delays such as DNS lookups during object reads with statistical gates for blind cases.
12266. **OOB-deserialization correlator** — requires token-correlated callbacks from gadget execution.
12267. **PHP-object-injection sink prover** — proves the injected object reaches a dangerous magic method such as wakeup or destruct, not merely that unserialization succeeded.
12268. **Python-pickle reduce prover** — confirms the pickle reduce opcode actually executes a callable during confirmation using a sandboxed canary.
12269. **Node-serialization function-revival check** — verifies functions actually revive rather than merely parse in JavaScript deserialization.
12270. **DotNET-serialization binder gate** — checks binder and type restrictions before claiming exploitability, since restricted binders kill most gadget chains.
12271. **JSON-versus-native separator** — plain JSON parsing is not deserialization, and type-tag or object-revival semantics are required.
12272. **JWT-deserialization confusion guard** — never confuses JWT parsing with object deserialization.
12273. **Deserialization denial-of-service qualifier** — labels deep-nesting and billion-laughs variants as denial-of-service class with measured impact rather than remote code execution.
12274. **HMAC-signed blob verifier** — checks for integrity protection on serialized blobs, since properly signed blobs are not attacker controlled.
12275. **Deserialization merge key** — findings merge on endpoint, serialization format, and gadget.
12276. **Canonical file-read proof** — requires reading a known canary file outside the web root, since not-found variations alone are never local file inclusion.
12277. **Traversal-depth measurer** — determines how many parent-directory segments are needed, and insufficient depth that never escapes is not a finding.
12278. **Wrapper-support prover** — for filter wrappers, proves the wrapper actually executes by returning base64 of a canary.
12279. **Log-poisoning versus LFI separator** — poisoned logs included through file inclusion need both primitives proven, since log content alone is not file inclusion.
12280. **Null-byte handling check** — verifies null-byte behavior matches the runtime version, since modern runtimes ignore null bytes.
12281. **Path-normalization audit** — tests whether the application normalizes parent segments before or after validation, since post-validation normalization is the real flaw.
12282. **RFI-egress prover** — remote file inclusion requires token-correlated fetching of the attacker URL, and mere URL acceptance without fetching stays unconfirmed.
12283. **File-extension enforcement tester** — verifies the enforced extension actually constrains reads through null-byte and double-extension tests rather than assuming.
12284. **Directory-listing versus traversal separator** — open directory listing is its own finding, and traversal needs file-content proof.
12285. **Windows-drive traversal check** — tests drive-letter and UNC paths specifically on Windows stacks.
12286. **Zip-slip entry validator** — for archive uploads, proves path traversal on extraction with a canary entry rather than relying on suspicious names alone.
12287. **Traversal merge key** — findings merge on endpoint, parameter, and file accessed.
12288. **Upload-execution prover** — requires the uploaded file to be retrievable and interpreted or executed, since stored-but-inert files are informational.
12289. **MIME-versus-content sniffer check** — verifies the server sniffs content rather than only extensions before claiming bypass, since extension-only checks need extension proof.
12290. **Polyglot-confirmation gate** — polyglot files must demonstrably execute as the claimed type on retrieval.
12291. **Double-extension tester** — confirms the server extension parsing matches the claim, since many stacks safely take the last extension.
12292. **Config-upload behavior prover** — proves an uploaded server configuration actually changes behavior through a canary header rather than merely showing upload success.
12293. **SVG-upload script prover** — SVG cross-site scripting needs script execution in the victim browser context on direct navigation rather than mere file storage.
12294. **CSV-formula injection validator** — confirms the formula executes in the target spreadsheet application, since many viewers do not evaluate on open.
12295. **Log-injection versus log-forgery separator** — newline injection needs a demonstrated integrity impact such as fake entries parsed by monitoring, not just reflected newlines.
12296. **Log-viewer HTML-escape check** — verifies the viewer actually renders injected HTML before claiming log-viewer cross-site scripting.
12297. **CRLF-header-injection prover** — requires the injected header to appear in the actual response headers rather than only in a request echo.
12298. **Response-splitting body prover** — proves a second response body is actually split, since modern servers reject bare carriage-return and line-feed characters.
12299. **SMTP-header injection validator** — confirms the injected header reaches the sent email at a canary recipient rather than only appearing in a form echo.
12300. **Host-header cache prover** — host-header poisoning needs cache-backed proof with the poisoned response served to a second client, not single-response reflection.
12301. **Password-reset poisoning prover** — requires the poisoned reset link to be delivered to a canary inbox, since header reflection alone stays unconfirmed.
12302. **Upload and parse merge hygiene** — merges upload-vector findings by endpoint, file type, and execution context.
12303. **Second-order upload trigger mapper** — identifies the later action such as admin preview or batch job that triggers the uploaded payload.
12304. **Parser-differential upload check** — verifies the server-side parser interprets the file dangerously rather than trusting the uploader claim.
12305. **Internal-IP timing-differential proof** — compares response timing and behavior for internal versus external versus unroutable IPs to prove the request actually egresses the server.
12306. **Metadata-endpoint canary proof** — requests the cloud metadata endpoint for a canary path returning non-sensitive data, and credential exfiltration is never performed during confirmation.
12307. **DNS-rebinding SSRF validator** — confirms DNS-rebinding primitives actually resolve to attacker-controlled addresses at request time rather than only at validation time.
12308. **Redirect-chain SSRF prover** — proves the fetcher follows redirects to internal targets, and validators that check then fetch differently are labeled as time-of-check versus time-of-use issues.
12309. **Expected-behavior baseline** — documents what URLs the endpoint legitimately fetches, and deviations from that baseline define the anomaly rather than absolute rules.
12310. **Scheme-restriction tester** — verifies which schemes the fetcher supports among HTTP, gopher, file, and dict protocols, and unsupported schemes are excluded from claims.
12311. **Localhost-bypass matrix** — tests loopback representations including decimal, hex, and octal encodings systematically, with each bypass confirmed as its own primitive.
12312. **Cloud-metadata version gate** — checks whether token-required metadata service versions mitigate the issue, and findings are labeled according to the actual version behavior.
12313. **SSRF-versus-open-redirect separator** — distinguishes server-side fetching from client-side redirects, since only the former qualifies as server-side request forgery.
12314. **Webhook-URL SSRF qualifier** — request forgery through webhook configuration needs proof the server fetches on trigger rather than merely storing the URL.
12315. **PDF-generator SSRF prover** — confirms the server-side renderer issues the request through token-correlated callbacks rather than the browser.
12316. **Image-proxy SSRF validator** — proves the proxy fetches internal URLs while documenting its content-type restrictions.
12317. **XXE-SSRF attributor** — attributes server-side requests triggered through XXE to the correct root cause.
12318. **Request-smuggling SSRF guard** — never confuses smuggled-request artifacts with server-side request forgery.
12319. **SSRF blind-timing proof** — uses response-time differentials for internal versus blackholed hosts with statistical gates.
12320. **Port-scan through SSRF limiter** — port enumeration is capped to a handful of canary ports, and full port scans are out of scope for confirmation.
12321. **SSRF merge key** — findings merge on endpoint, parameter, and egress-target class.
12322. **Egress-filter detector** — detects egress filtering and labels findings as filtered rather than claiming full request forgery.
12323. **DNS-exfil versus HTTP-exfil separator** — labels the exfiltration channel actually proven rather than assuming one.
12324. **SSRF fix re-verification** — replays the exact bypass encoding after a fix rather than a weaker variant.
12325. **Two-account differential proof** — the same object must be accessible to the non-owner account with a reproducible differential, since single-account access proves nothing.
12326. **Owner-versus-nonowner response comparator** — diffs full responses rather than only status codes, since applications often return 200 with an error body.
12327. **Error-body versus data discriminator** — access returning an error JSON document is not insecure direct object reference, and actual object data is required.
12328. **Predictable-ID enumerability sampler** — samples a small identifier range to prove sequential predictability, since theoretical predictability without sampling stays unconfirmed.
12329. **UUID-unguessability verifier** — measures identifier entropy, and high-entropy unguessable identifiers earn a low-exploitability label even when technically referenceable.
12330. **Indirect-reference mapper** — maps indirect references such as hashes and slugs to prove they do not leak the direct identifier.
12331. **Cross-role access matrix** — tests every role against every object class, and findings are reported per role-and-object pair that actually leaks.
12332. **Function-level access prover** — hidden endpoints need proof of invocation with real effect rather than a mere 200 response on GET.
12333. **HTTP-method override tester** — verifies method-override headers actually change authorization outcomes.
12334. **Mass-assignment versus IDOR separator** — distinguishes writable-field abuse from readable-object abuse because each deserves its own finding.
12335. **IDOR-on-write prover** — write-side reference flaws need proof of modification through a canary field flip plus revert rather than a mere 200 OK.
12336. **Non-destructive write canary** — write proofs modify only a canary field and immediately revert, with the revert itself verified.
12337. **Bulk-enumeration feasibility estimator** — estimates records per minute and total exposure window, and infeasible enumeration is labeled accordingly.
12338. **Rate-limit IDOR gate** — checks whether rate limiting makes mass enumeration infeasible in practice.
12339. **Stale-cache IDOR guard** — rules out cached responses from another user session masquerading as insecure direct object reference.
12340. **Shared-device session artifact filter** — excludes findings caused by test accounts sharing browser state.
12341. **Tenant-isolation prover** — for multi-tenant applications, proves cross-tenant access specifically, since same-tenant access may be by design.
12342. **Public-by-design excluder** — excludes objects the application intentionally makes public such as shared links and public profiles through feature-flag analysis.
12343. **Soft-delete visibility check** — verifies whether deleted objects are intentionally visible through trash and restore interfaces before claiming reference flaws.
12344. **API-version authorization drift** — tests old API versions for missing authorization checks that newer versions enforce.
12345. **GraphQL-IDOR field prover** — proves the unauthorized field actually resolves data rather than merely appearing in the schema.
12346. **WebSocket authorization validator** — confirms subscription channels enforce authorization per topic, with cross-user message receipt as proof.
12347. **IDOR merge key** — findings merge on object type, endpoint, and victim role.
12348. **Authorization-fix re-verification** — replays both accounts requests after a fix is claimed.
12349. **Privilege-escalation chain gate** — privilege escalation is claimed only when the higher-privileged action demonstrably succeeds.
12350. **Credential-enumeration differential gate** — username enumeration needs statistically significant user-versus-nonuser differentials across both message content and timing.
12351. **Timing-enumeration jitter guard** — login timing differences must exceed network jitter baselines, and sub-fifty-millisecond differences on remote targets are rejected.
12352. **Generic-message verifier** — confirms the application messages are actually identical at byte level before ruling out enumeration.
12353. **Password-reset token entropy audit** — measures reset-token entropy, and low-entropy tokens need a guessing-feasibility proof rather than a looks-short judgment.
12354. **Token-expiry enforcement test** — verifies expired tokens are actually rejected, since non-expiry is the finding rather than token format.
12355. **Host-header reset-link prover** — requires the reset email at a canary inbox to contain the poisoned link, since header reflection alone stays unconfirmed.
12356. **Two-factor bypass state-machine proof** — proves the authenticated state is reached without the second factor through a minted session cookie rather than mere interface skipping.
12357. **Backup-code brute-force feasibility** — estimates attempts needed versus rate limits before claiming backup-code weakness.
12358. **Session-fixation prover** — proves the pre-login session identifier remains valid after login, since session rotation kills the finding.
12359. **Concurrent-session control tester** — verifies whether the application actually enforces its single-session promises.
12360. **Logout-invalidation verifier** — proves logout invalidates server side, since client-side cookie deletion alone is insufficient.
12361. **Session-entropy measurer** — measures session identifier entropy, and predictable identifiers need a prediction demonstration.
12362. **Cookie-tossing versus fixation separator** — distinguishes subdomain cookie tossing from true session fixation.
12363. **OAuth redirect-uri validator** — proves the redirect URI bypass actually delivers codes to an attacker origin through a canary rather than merely accepting the parameter.
12364. **OAuth state-parameter gate** — verifies state is absent or unvalidated and the flow is actually exploitable through login cross-site request forgery.
12365. **PKCE-enforcement check** — verifies the code challenge is actually validated server side.
12366. **JWT none-algorithm acceptance proof** — forges an algorithm-none token and proves privileged access, since library support without acceptance is not a finding.
12367. **JWT weak-secret crack gate** — cracks only with a small dictionary and proves the cracked key signs accepted tokens, since weak-looking alone is not proof.
12368. **JWT key-id traversal prover** — proves the key-id path actually reads attacker-influenced keys through a canary file rather than merely exhibiting path-like behavior.
12369. **JWT key-URL SSRF prover** — requires token-correlated fetching of the attacker key URL for key-URL header flaws.
12370. **JWT expiry-ignored test** — proves expired tokens are accepted, since a missing expiry claim alone is informational.
12371. **Auth-bypass versus auth-bug separator** — distinguishes complete bypass from logic bugs needing chaining, and severity follows the proof.
12372. **Default-credential blast limiter** — tests only documented default pairs and never brute forces, with success constituting the finding.
12373. **Credential-stuffing guard** — the agent never performs credential stuffing, and stuffing feasibility is assessed through rate-limit analysis only.
12374. **Auth merge key** — findings merge on authentication flow, endpoint, and bypass primitive.
12375. **API-key scope verifier** — proves the key accesses out-of-scope resources rather than merely proving the key exists.
12376. **Key-rotation staleness check** — verifies old keys are actually rejected after rotation.
12377. **Service-account privilege prover** — proves the service account effective permissions through canary actions.
12378. **Impersonation-feature audit** — distinguishes legitimate admin impersonation features with audit logs from insecure direct object reference.
12379. **Audit-log presence check** — verifies privileged actions are logged, and unlogged admin actions compound the finding severity.
12380. **Password-change CSRF gate** — proves the state-changing request lacks token protection and actually executes.
12381. **Email-change verification gap** — proves email can be changed without re-verification and the new address receives privileged communications.
12382. **Account-deletion authorization check** — proves non-owners cannot trigger deletion, since buttons hidden in the interface do not prove server-side authorization.
12383. **Invite-token reuse tester** — proves invite and registration tokens are actually reusable or predictable.
12384. **CAPTCHA-bypass necessity test** — determines whether CAPTCHA is enforced server side as opposed to client side only.
12385. **Rate-limit auth gate** — brute-force findings need measured attempt ceilings rather than assumed ones.
12386. **Account-lockout differential** — verifies lockout actually triggers and whether it enables user enumeration or denial of service.
12387. **SAML signature verifier** — proves assertions without valid signatures are accepted through a forged assertion carrying a canary.
12388. **SAML recipient-audience check** — verifies audience and recipient validation, and missing validation needs a cross-provider proof.
12389. **OIDC issuer-confusion test** — proves the application accepts tokens from a rogue issuer through a canary issuer rather than relying on documentation claims.
12390. **Subdomain-cookie-scope audit** — verifies cookie domain scope actually enables session riding from the compromised subdomain.
12391. **Cookie-prefix enforcement check** — verifies Host and Secure cookie prefixes are actually enforced by the claimed application logic.
12392. **Session-pinning detector** — detects device and session pinning that mitigates stolen-cookie impact, and findings are labeled with pinning status.
12393. **Refresh-token rotation verifier** — proves refresh tokens are actually rotated with reuse detection, since non-rotation is the finding.
12394. **Token-binding check** — verifies proof-of-possession or mutual-TLS binding is enforced rather than merely advertised.
12395. **Biometric-fallback tester** — verifies fallback authentication such as PIN or SMS is not weaker than the primary method, since weaker fallback is the finding.
12396. **Magic-link entropy and expiry** — measures magic-link entropy and verifies single-use and expiry enforcement.
12397. **Registration-race prover** — proves duplicate-registration races actually create inconsistent state through canary accounts.
12398. **Username-squatting similarity guard** — distinguishes lookalike-username social vectors from technical vulnerabilities and labels them rather than scoring them as high-severity flaws.
12399. **Deprovisioning lag check** — verifies departed users tokens are actually revoked, and the lag window is measured.
12400. **Privilege-cache invalidation test** — verifies role changes propagate, and cached-privilege windows are measured in minutes.
12401. **API-authorization parity check** — verifies mobile and API endpoints enforce the same authorization as web, since parity gaps are the finding.
12402. **Webhook-secret verifier** — proves webhook signatures are actually validated, since tampered payload acceptance is the finding.
12403. **HMAC-timing side-channel gate** — timing attacks need statistical significance over network jitter, and local-only nanosecond differences do not transfer to remote findings.
12404. **Auth-confidence combiner** — fuses multi-signal authentication findings into one calibrated confidence score.
12405. **State-change plus token-absence prover** — cross-site request forgery needs a demonstrably executed state change through a canary with no valid token, since a token present in the proof of concept invalidates it.
12406. **SameSite actual-behavior test** — verifies the cookie real SameSite enforcement in a cross-site test page rather than trusting the attribute value alone.
12407. **GET-based state-change qualifier** — labels GET-triggered changes as request forgery only when they are genuinely state changing, since analytics GET requests are not.
12408. **Token-validation prover** — proves the token is actually validated because wrong-token acceptance is the finding, while mere token existence means nothing.
12409. **Referer and Origin-check bypass tester** — verifies the actual validation logic of referer checks, since naive substring checks need a demonstrated bypass.
12410. **Double-submit consistency check** — verifies the two submitted tokens are actually compared server side.
12411. **CSRF-on-login qualifier** — login request forgery needs a demonstrated impact such as account linking rather than mere form submission.
12412. **JSON-CSRF content-type gate** — proves the endpoint accepts the smuggled content type, since text-plain preflight behavior must be tested rather than assumed.
12413. **CORS-and-CSRF interaction audit** — verifies whether permissive cross-origin policies already nullify request-forgery protections to avoid double reporting.
12414. **Multi-step CSRF chain prover** — multi-step flows need end-to-end execution proof because intermediate tokens frequently break the chain.
12415. **CSRF merge key** — findings merge on endpoint, action, and absent protection.
12416. **SameSite-None plus Secure audit** — verifies the cookie combination is actually set as claimed.
12417. **Token-per-session versus per-request** — determines token granularity, since per-request tokens that are never validated remain a finding.
12418. **CSRF-fix re-verification** — replays the proof of concept after a fix using the previously valid session.
12419. **Logout-CSRF impact labeler** — labels logout request forgery as low impact explicitly rather than inflating it.
12420. **External-navigation prover** — open redirect needs actual cross-origin navigation in a real browser rather than a mere Location header containing a URL.
12421. **Allowlist-bypass demonstrator** — bypasses need a working bypass URL rather than a suspicious-looking regular expression.
12422. **JavaScript-scheme gate** — verifies the javascript scheme actually executes in the redirect context, since many contexts neuter it.
12423. **Redirect-chain-to-OAuth prover** — OAuth token-theft chains need end-to-end proof with canary tokens.
12424. **Open-redirect merge key** — findings merge on endpoint, parameter, and bypass technique.
12425. **Credentialed-CORS read prover** — cross-origin findings need actual cross-origin credentialed reads of sensitive data, since wildcard origins without credentials are informational.
12426. **Null-origin gate** — verifies the application actually reflects a null origin and the browser sends it in the real attack context.
12427. **Trusted-subdomain CORS audit** — proves the trusted subdomain is actually attacker compromisable through takeover or scripting before escalating severity.
12428. **Vary-Origin cache guard** — checks whether cross-origin responses are cached and poisonable.
12429. **CORS merge key** — findings merge on endpoint and origin-policy flaw.
12430. **Frameable-plus-actionable clickjacking prover** — needs the page frameable and a sensitive one-click action present, since missing frame options alone are not the finding.
12431. **Frame-busting-code tester** — verifies the frame-busting code actually executes and is not neutered by sandbox attributes.
12432. **Drag-and-drop action prover** — drag-based vectors need a working drag-to-action demonstration since most are impractical.
12433. **postMessage-origin prover** — proves cross-origin messages reach the sink, since same-origin listeners are excluded.
12434. **postMessage merge key** — findings merge on listener, sink, and absent origin check.
12435. **CSWSH origin prover** — cross-site WebSocket hijacking needs an actual cross-origin connection performing actions, since a missing Origin check alone is insufficient.
12436. **WebSocket-authorization topic prover** — proves cross-user topic subscription actually delivers messages.
12437. **GraphQL-introspection exposure measurer** — measures the fraction of schema actually exposed rather than treating introspection as a binary on-off finding.
12438. **GraphQL-batching brute-force feasibility** — estimates attack attempts versus rate limits for batched attacks.
12439. **Field-suggestion info-leak qualifier** — labels suggestions as information leaks only when they reveal non-public fields.
12440. **GraphQL merge key** — findings merge on endpoint and flaw class.
12441. **Cache-poisoning two-client prover** — requires the poisoned response served to a second clean client, since single-client anomalies are not cache poisoning.
12442. **Cache-key injection demonstrator** — proves the injected key component actually busts or poisons the cache entry.
12443. **Cache-buster hygiene** — all cache tests use unique busting parameters to avoid self-poisoning artifacts.
12444. **Request-smuggling desync prover** — needs a demonstrably desynchronized second request carrying a canary prefix, since timing anomalies alone stay unconfirmed.
12445. **CL.TE versus TE.CL attributor** — attributes the exact variant proven, and unproven variants are never reported.
12446. **Smuggling safe-prefix discipline** — uses safe methods and prefixes that cannot harm other users requests during confirmation.
12447. **Race-window measurer** — measures the exploit window in milliseconds and requires demonstrated double-spend or state corruption with canary values.
12448. **Rate-limit versus race separator** — distinguishes rate-limit gaps from true race conditions through single-packet techniques.
12449. **Prototype-pollution sink prover** — proves the polluted property reaches a dangerous sink, since pollution of inert properties is informational.
12450. **Git-exposure completeness measurer** — measures the fraction of repository objects actually retrievable, and partial exposure is labeled rather than assumed complete.
12451. **Env-content redactor** — confirms environment-file exposure through canary keys while redacting real secrets in evidence.
12452. **Stack-trace intelligence qualifier** — scores traces by actionable content rather than mere presence.
12453. **Backup-file partial-inspection cap** — inspects only headers and file lists of exposed backups and never full dumps.
12454. **Subdomain-takeover claimability gate** — proves the external service actually allows claiming the dangling name, since non-claimable dangling DNS is informational.
12455. **Takeover non-claiming discipline** — never actually claims the resource during confirmation, and claimability is proven through the provider API or documentation check.
12456. **Secret-entropy plus context validator** — high-entropy strings need surrounding context such as key names or active prefixes before being labeled secrets.
12457. **Active-secret verification without use** — verifies secrets through provider validation APIs or metadata rather than by using the secret.
12458. **Canary-secret planter** — plants a canary secret to test detection pipelines without touching real ones.
12459. **Info-disclosure aggregation gate** — aggregation needs a demonstrated combined exploit path rather than a mere list of leaks.
12460. **Version-leak reachability check** — version strings need a reachable CVE to matter, since version disclosure alone is informational.
12461. **Directory-indexing sensitivity audit** — lists what is actually exposed rather than merely noting that indexing is enabled.
12462. **Source-map exposure analyzer** — verifies the map actually maps to original source rather than merely noting the file exists.
12463. **Debug-endpoint action prover** — debug endpoints need a demonstrated dangerous action rather than mere exposure.
12464. **Health-check info qualifier** — labels health endpoints by the data sensitivity actually returned.
12465. **TLS-handshake capture proof** — weak TLS needs an actual negotiated weak-handshake capture rather than a configuration claim.
12466. **Cipher-suite practicality gate** — a weak cipher needs a feasible attack rather than a theoretical one or it stays informational.
12467. **Certificate-validity checker** — verifies actual chain, expiry, and hostname failures through handshakes rather than scanner heuristics.
12468. **HSTS-preload versus header distinguisher** — labels preload and header-only policies correctly since header-only HSTS has known limits.
12469. **Missing-header impact gate** — missing security headers are reported only with a demonstrated bypass they enable.
12470. **Cookie-flag MITM practicality** — a missing Secure flag needs a realistic man-in-the-middle or adjacent-network scenario and is labeled accordingly.
12471. **HttpOnly-bypass necessity** — HttpOnly absence matters only when scripting is proven, and standalone it is defense in depth.
12472. **Dangerous-method prover** — methods such as TRACE, TRACK, and PUT need demonstrated dangerous behavior rather than mere method acceptance.
12473. **Method-override authorization recheck** — verifies override headers actually change authorization outcomes.
12474. **Host-header single-versus-cache separator** — single-response reflection without cache impact is low severity.
12475. **DOM-clobbering gadget prover** — needs the gadget script present and the clobbered value reaching a sink.
12476. **JSONP-callback hijack prover** — needs an actual cross-origin data-theft demonstration with canary data.
12477. **JSONP-removed qualifier** — verifies JSONP is actually still active rather than dead code.
12478. **AngularJS-expression sandbox gate** — verifies the framework version sandbox status before claiming expression injection.
12479. **Vue and React XSS sink audit** — verifies the framework escaping at the exact sink version in use.
12480. **jQuery-version sink gate** — old jQuery sinks need the vulnerable library version actually loaded.
12481. **Third-party-script audit** — verifies the third-party script is actually loaded and its compromise would matter.
12482. **SRI-absence impact gate** — missing subresource integrity matters only for high-risk third parties and is labeled accordingly.
12483. **Mixed-content active-versus-passive separator** — active mixed content is the finding while passive images are informational.
12484. **Referrer-policy leak prover** — proves sensitive data actually leaks through the Referer header to third parties.
12485. **Tabnabbing opener gate** — verifies window opener is actually exploitable through absent noopener protections in the real context.
12486. **Download-attribute drive-by check** — verifies the download actually triggers without user consent in the claimed browser.
12487. **Notification-API abuse qualifier** — labels by required permissions since permission-gated APIs are low severity.
12488. **Geolocation-permission gate** — verifies the permission-prompt behavior, since denied-by-default is not a finding.
12489. **WebRTC-IP-leak practicality** — verifies the leak occurs in default browser configurations, and extension-blocked leaks are labeled.
12490. **Clipboard-access prover** — proves programmatic clipboard reads without user gesture.
12491. **Fullscreen-UI-redress prover** — needs a demonstrated convincing phishing scenario rather than mere API availability.
12492. **Sensor-API privacy qualifier** — labels by the actual privacy impact demonstrated.
12493. **Payment-API abuse gate** — verifies the API actually processes without user confirmation.
12494. **Credential-management API audit** — verifies silent credential access is actually possible.
12495. **Bluetooth and USB device gate** — verifies the device chooser cannot be bypassed silently.
12496. **File-System-Access API prover** — proves silent file writes without a picker dialog.
12497. **PWA-install prompt abuse qualifier** — labels by the required user gestures.
12498. **Push-notification spam gate** — verifies subscription without visible permission.
12499. **Background-sync abuse check** — verifies synchronization actually exfiltrates without user awareness.
12500. **Client-side finding merge key** — findings merge on page, sink, and vector.
12501. **Browser-matrix confirmation** — records the confirming browser and engine versions.
12502. **Client-side fix re-verification** — replays the exact proof of concept after a fix.
12503. **Interaction-required labeler** — consistently labels user-interaction dependencies across all findings.
12504. **Defense-in-depth versus vulnerability separator** — distinguishes missing hardening labeled informational from exploitable flaws labeled as findings through a documented rubric, preventing hardening checklists from masquerading as vulnerability reports.
12505. **Per-class base-rate priors** — seeds each vulnerability class with its historical confirmation rate so novel claims start skeptical rather than at fifty-fifty.
12506. **Likelihood-ratio evidence weighting** — each probe type contributes a likelihood ratio of true-positive rate over false-positive rate instead of flat points.
12507. **Posterior-threshold promotion** — findings promote to confirmed only at posterior of at least point nine five and to probable at point eight, keeping the math explicit.
12508. **Prior-updating from program history** — priors shift per target program based on its historical false-positive rate, so noisy programs start more skeptical.
12509. **Class-conditional prior refinement** — priors split by fine context such as reflected scripting in JavaScript strings versus in HTML, since base rates differ wildly.
12510. **Evidence-independence discount** — correlated evidence from the same oracle or code path receives a correlation penalty before fusion.
12511. **Sequential Bayesian updating** — confidence updates probe by probe with a running posterior so the agent can stop early when thresholds are crossed.
12512. **Prior-robustness check** — re-computes the posterior under pessimistic priors, and findings that survive earn a prior-robust label.
12513. **Base-rate fallacy guard** — blocks the impressive-probe impossible-bug pattern by requiring extraordinary claims such as remote code execution to carry proportionally stronger evidence.
12514. **Hierarchical priors** — priors nest across program, asset, endpoint, and parameter levels so a historically clean endpoint starts more skeptical.
12515. **Prior-decay for new code** — recently changed endpoints get less benefit from historical priors since the slate is effectively clean.
12516. **Empirical-Bayes calibration** — priors are fit from the agent own confirmation history rather than guessed.
12517. **Prior-transparency record** — every finding stores the prior used so reviewers can audit the starting skepticism.
12518. **Adversarial-prior stress test** — re-scores top findings under hostile priors to expose conclusions that hinge on optimistic assumptions.
12519. **Prior-versus-evidence contribution split** — reports how much final confidence came from prior versus evidence, flagging prior-driven confirmations.
12520. **Cold-start prior protocol** — brand-new vulnerability classes use a conservative point-one prior until fifty labeled cases exist.
12521. **Prior-override audit** — any manual prior override is logged with justification and reviewer identity.
12522. **Multi-program prior pooling** — pools priors across programs with similarity weighting to avoid single-program overfitting.
12523. **Prior half-life** — old historical data decays in prior computation so the last quarter counts more than last year.
12524. **Prior-predictive check** — simulates expected confirmation counts from priors and flags hunts that deviate wildly as broken detectors or broken priors.
12525. **Confidence half-life decay** — un-reverified findings lose half their confidence every seven days, forcing re-verification or demotion.
12526. **Evidence-freshness weighting** — probe evidence decays exponentially with age so a thirty-day-old proof counts less than yesterday proof.
12527. **Re-verification refresh** — a fresh successful re-probe resets the decay clock to full confidence.
12528. **Decay-pause for fixed findings** — remediated findings stop decaying and archive at their final state.
12529. **Environment-change decay trigger** — deploys or configuration changes on the target instantly halve confidence pending re-verification.
12530. **Dempster-Shafer evidence fusion** — combines independent probe beliefs with explicit ignorance modeling instead of naive averaging.
12531. **Weighted-voter fusion** — each technique votes with weight equal to its historical precision, and the majority of weight rather than count decides.
12532. **Contradiction-resolution protocol** — when probes disagree, the finding drops to contested with disagreeing transcripts preserved rather than silently outvoted.
12533. **Diminishing-returns evidence cap** — the fifth identical-probe success adds less than one percent confidence, since repetition is not corroboration.
12534. **Oracle-diversity bonus** — confidence jumps only when a second different oracle agrees, so time-based plus out-of-band beats time-based plus time-based.
12535. **Negative-evidence integration** — failed probes are first-class evidence that lowers confidence rather than being ignored as inconclusive runs.
12536. **Absence-of-evidence labeler** — distinguishes tested-and-absent which lowers confidence from not-tested which changes nothing.
12537. **Confidence-interval reporting** — reports ninety-percent intervals such as point eight two to point nine four instead of point estimates, making uncertainty visible.
12538. **Monte-Carlo confidence simulation** — samples uncertain parameters like jitter and priors ten thousand times to produce the interval honestly.
12539. **Sensitivity analysis per finding** — identifies which single assumption the conclusion hinges on and stress-tests it.
12540. **Evidence-graph visualization** — renders the probe-to-conclusion dependency graph so reviewers see exactly what supports what.
12541. **Circular-evidence detector** — flags when probe B validity assumes probe A conclusion, blocking bootstrapped confirmations.
12542. **Double-counting guard** — prevents the same underlying observation from one response feeding two supposedly independent probes.
12543. **Conditional-independence audit** — documents why two probes are treated as independent, and unjustified independence claims are downgraded.
12544. **Fusion-formula versioning** — the exact fusion math version is stored per finding so old scores stay interpretable.
12545. **Confidence-floor for auto-report** — nothing below point nine posterior reaches the client report without human sign-off.
12546. **Confidence-ceiling for single-probe** — no single probe however strong can exceed point eight five alone, making corroboration mandatory.
12547. **Time-to-confidence estimator** — predicts probes needed to cross thresholds so the agent budgets verification effort.
12548. **Early-stopping rule** — probing stops when additional probes cannot mathematically cross the next threshold because the value of information is near zero.
12549. **Probe-budget allocator** — distributes verification probes by expected information gain rather than round robin.
12550. **Predicted-versus-empirical calibration curve** — plots binned predicted confidence against actual reviewer confirmation rates every month.
12551. **Calibration-drift alarm** — alerts when the curve deviates into overconfidence beyond tolerance, triggering threshold retuning.
12552. **Per-class calibration** — curves are computed per vulnerability class since scripting and request-forgery calibrate differently.
12553. **Per-technique precision tracking** — every probe technique precision is tracked, and sub-point-five techniques are quarantined.
12554. **Reviewer-agreement calibration** — compares agent confidence against inter-reviewer agreement, and low-agreement classes get wider intervals.
12555. **Brier-score tracking** — scores the confidence system with Brier scores over time, where lower is better and regressions page the team.
12556. **Reliability-diagram publishing** — includes the calibration diagram in internal quality reports for transparency.
12557. **Overconfidence-penalty tuner** — automatically widens intervals for classes with historical overconfidence.
12558. **Underconfidence detector** — flags classes where high-confidence predictions are always right but rare, indicating too-timid thresholds.
12559. **Calibration-by-severity** — verifies Critical-labeled findings are actually confirmed at Critical-worthy rates.
12560. **Temporal calibration stability** — checks calibration does not degrade as the target evolves, and drift triggers re-baselining.
12561. **Cross-program calibration transfer** — tests whether calibration holds on new programs before trusting it there.
12562. **Confidence-audit sampling** — samples findings across the confidence spectrum for blind re-review every month.
12563. **Score-explanation fidelity check** — verifies the human-readable why text actually matches the math that produced the score.
12564. **Rounding-discipline rule** — confidences report to two decimals maximum, and false precision such as five decimals is banned.
12565. **Confidence-versus-severity separation audit** — ensures severity is not smuggled into confidence or vice versa.
12566. **Threshold-justification record** — every promotion threshold has a documented cost-benefit justification.
12567. **Cost-of-FP versus cost-of-FN model** — thresholds derive from explicit false-positive and false-negative cost estimates per program rather than intuition.
12568. **Threshold-per-program tuning** — high-noise programs get higher auto-report thresholds.
12569. **Emergency-threshold override** — critical-infrastructure targets get lower auto-escalation thresholds that are documented and audited.
12570. **Threshold-change changelog** — every threshold change is versioned with before-and-after impact analysis.
12571. **A/B threshold experiments** — threshold changes are tested on shadow traffic before production rollout.
12572. **Confidence-compression guard** — prevents all findings clustering at point nine nine, since healthy systems show a spread.
12573. **Zero-evidence confidence ban** — findings with no probe evidence cannot exceed point three no matter how alarming the heuristic.
12574. **Heuristic-only labeler** — heuristic detections stay permanently labeled heuristic until probe evidence arrives.
12575. **Unknown-unknown reserve** — reserves an unmodeled-risk term so confidence never reaches exactly one point zero.
12576. **Model-uncertainty versus data-uncertainty split** — separates uncertainty about the math from noisy data in the report.
12577. **Adversarial-noise margin** — widens intervals for targets with active WAFs or adversarial responses.
12578. **Small-sample warning** — findings with fewer than five probes get a small-sample badge regardless of score.
12579. **Multiple-comparison correction** — when a thousand parameters are probed, significance thresholds tighten in Bonferroni style to control false-positive floods.
12580. **Look-elsewhere effect guard** — the more probes run, the stronger the final evidence must be, penalizing significance hunting through probing.
12581. **Stopping-rule bias correction** — accounts for probing having stopped exactly when significance appeared, correcting optional-stopping inflation.
12582. **Regression-to-the-mean guard** — extreme first-probe results are re-tested before belief since flukes regress.
12583. **Survivorship-bias audit** — tracks probes that were started but abandoned, since abandoned-probe patterns reveal systematic blind spots.
12584. **Selection-bias corrector** — adjusts for the agent probing interesting endpoints more heavily, since interesting does not equal vulnerable.
12585. **Confirmation-bias circuit breaker** — after three failed confirmations the agent must switch techniques or drop the hypothesis rather than keep hammering.
12586. **Sunk-cost probe limiter** — caps probes per hypothesis because having tried fifty payloads is not evidence.
12587. **Hypothesis-registry** — every hypothesis is registered before probing, and unregistered discoveries are treated as exploratory rather than confirmatory.
12588. **Pre-registered success criteria** — the confirmation bar is set before probing starts, preventing moving goalposts.
12589. **Exploratory-versus-confirmatory labeler** — reconnaissance-phase hunches stay labeled exploratory until a pre-registered confirmatory test passes.
12590. **HARKing detector** — flags hypotheses clearly formed after seeing the data and requires fresh-data confirmation.
12591. **Out-of-sample confirmation** — the confirming probe must use data and payloads not used during hypothesis formation.
12592. **Cross-validation for ML detectors** — machine-learning detectors are evaluated with proper cross-validation rather than training-set accuracy.
12593. **Detector-precision floor** — any detector below point seven precision is demoted to hint generator and never acts as a confirmer.
12594. **Ensemble-diversity metric** — measures whether ensemble members actually disagree sometimes, since clones add no value.
12595. **Confidence-backtest harness** — replays historical hunts through new confidence math to measure improvement before rollout.
12596. **Counterfactual-confidence check** — asks what confidence would be if the strongest probe were removed, and fragile findings are flagged.
12597. **Leave-one-probe-out robustness** — findings must survive removal of their strongest probe to earn a robust label.
12598. **Adversarial-evidence injection test** — tests whether a single malicious response could manufacture a false confirmation, probing the robustness of the math itself.
12599. **Confidence-math documentation standard** — every formula has a documentation page with assumptions, limits, and worked examples.
12600. **Uncertainty-budget report** — the PDF shows where uncertainty comes from, for example probe noise forty percent and prior thirty percent.
12601. **Decision-theoretic reporting rule** — reports include findings when expected value of impact times confidence exceeds the review cost.
12602. **Value-of-information probe ordering** — next probes are chosen by expected information gain per request cost.
12603. **Optimal-stopping for verification** — a formal stopping rule balances probe cost against false-positive cost.
12604. **Confidence-math peer review** — changes to the confidence math require a second-engineer review before deployment.
12605. **WAF-block-page fingerprint library** — maintains signatures for over forty WAF products so payload echoes in block pages are never mistaken for genuine reflections.
12606. **Block-page versus app-page discriminator** — compares response headers, titles, and DOM structure to decide whether the suspicious response came from the WAF at all.
12607. **WAF-echo quarantine** — any finding whose only evidence is WAF-echoed payload is auto-quarantined with the WAF signature attached.
12608. **Challenge-page detector** — identifies JavaScript and captcha bot-management challenges and excludes their echoed payloads from analysis.
12609. **Rate-limit-page discriminator** — fingerprints 429 pages so SQL keywords in rate-limit responses are not misread as error-based SQLi.
12610. **WAF-learning-mode detector** — detects WAFs in monitoring-only mode through header analysis to avoid assuming protection that is not active.
12611. **WAF-rule-ID extractor** — parses block pages for rule identifiers, and repeated rule IDs reveal which payload classes are filtered, guiding rather than faking confirmation.
12612. **False-block versus true-block separator** — distinguishes WAF blocks of the probe from application-level rejections, since only application behavior counts toward confirmation.
12613. **CDN-error-page library** — fingerprints major CDN error pages that echo request data.
12614. **Edge-redirect artifact filter** — excludes redirect responses generated at the edge rather than the application from open-redirect analysis.
12615. **Bot-score header auditor** — reads bot-management headers to know when responses are bot-tailored, discounting their evidence accordingly.
12616. **WAF-bypass versus WAF-absent labeler** — labels whether the payload succeeded because the WAF was bypassed or because no WAF inspected that path.
12617. **API-gateway error discriminator** — fingerprints gateway errors from common gateways that mimic application errors.
12618. **Load-balancer error filter** — excludes load-balancer-generated 502 and 503 pages from injection analysis.
12619. **WAF-canary probe** — sends a known-blocked canary first to map exactly what the WAF inspects, calibrating all later probes.
12620. **Geo-block page detector** — identifies geo-blocking pages so region-dependent behaviors are not reported as global vulnerabilities.
12621. **IP-reputation block discriminator** — distinguishes reputation-based blocks from vulnerability-relevant behavior.
12622. **WAF-response-time fingerprint** — uses WAF-specific timing to attribute slow responses to the WAF rather than to time-based injection.
12623. **Managed-ruleset version tracker** — tracks WAF ruleset versions, and finding validity is re-checked whenever rulesets change.
12624. **WAF-evasion necessity audit** — documents whether evasion was needed, and findings requiring exotic evasion get an evasion-dependent label.
12625. **False-positive WAF-rule reporter** — when a WAF rule blocks benign application functionality, reports it as a tuning issue rather than an application vulnerability.
12626. **WAF-header presence versus enforcement** — verifies the WAF actually blocks rather than merely adding headers before crediting it as mitigation.
12627. **Multi-CDN attribution** — attributes each response to the serving CDN layer so findings are filed against the correct component.
12628. **Edge-compute behavior mapper** — maps edge-worker transformations that alter payloads before the application sees them.
12629. **Anycast-routing variance guard** — accounts for anycast routing sending probes to different points of presence with different behaviors.
12630. **Stale-edge-cache guard** — verifies findings against origin with cache busters, and edge-cached anomalies are excluded.
12631. **WAF-log versus app-log correlator** — correlates block events with application logs to confirm which layer acted.
12632. **Shadow-WAF detector** — detects WAFs that only log without blocking to prevent false mitigation credit.
12633. **WAF-fingerprint confidence** — the WAF identification itself carries a confidence score, and low-confidence identifications do not trigger exclusions.
12634. **Environment-attribution summary** — every finding records which layers among WAF, CDN, and application touched the probe path.
12635. **Framework-debug-page library** — fingerprints major framework debug pages so their verbose output is not mistaken for information-disclosure vulnerabilities.
12636. **Debug-mode qualifier** — labels findings from debug-mode responses as environment dependent and requires production-mode re-confirmation.
12637. **Default-error-page catalog** — catalogs framework default 404 and 500 pages to exclude their supposed leaks, which are merely defaults.
12638. **Dev-toolbar detector** — identifies framework debug toolbars, treating their presence as a configuration note and their data as non-evidence.
12639. **Example-app detector** — fingerprints framework example applications and welcome pages, excluding their intentionally vulnerable-looking demos.
12640. **Docs-page excluder** — auto-excludes documentation and API specification paths from vulnerability analysis since they are meant to be descriptive.
12641. **Health-check excluder** — excludes health, readiness, and ping endpoints from finding generation.
12642. **Actuator-endpoint qualifier** — actuator findings require actual sensitive exposure, since mere actuator exposure is a configuration note.
12643. **GraphQL-playground detector** — playground interfaces are developer tools, and their presence alone is not a finding.
12644. **Default-credential-page discriminator** — distinguishes default login pages from actual default-credential acceptance, which needs a login proof.
12645. **Installer-wizard detector** — identifies installer and setup wizards, treating their presence as a configuration finding only when actually executable.
12646. **phpinfo exposure qualifier** — phpinfo output is information disclosure only when it reveals non-public secrets, and the page itself is a hardening note.
12647. **Server-status page audit** — server-status endpoints need actual sensitive data rather than merely having status modules enabled.
12648. **Stack-trace default versus custom** — default framework traces carry lower severity than custom traces leaking business data.
12649. **Version-header catalog** — server and powered-by headers are cataloged as hardening notes and never as vulnerabilities alone.
12650. **Default-file excluder** — excludes robots files, favicons, and well-known URIs from anomaly-detection baselines.
12651. **Framework-migration artifact detector** — identifies half-migrated stacks showing headers from two frameworks to avoid misattribution.
12652. **CMS-version fingerprint gate** — CMS vulnerabilities need version-specific proof rather than version detection alone.
12653. **Plugin-enumeration prudence** — enumerated plugins are leads rather than findings until a vulnerable version with a reachable flaw is proven.
12654. **Theme-editor exposure check** — CMS theme editors need an actual file-write proof rather than mere menu visibility.
12655. **JSON user-enumeration qualifier** — user-listing API endpoints are by design on many sites, and the finding needs a demonstrated abuse path.
12656. **XMLRPC-method audit** — XML-RPC endpoints need a working abusive-method proof rather than mere existence.
12657. **Admin-ajax action enumerator** — enumerates ajax actions but requires per-action authorization proof.
12658. **Default-API-key detector** — distinguishes example keys in documentation from live keys.
12659. **Sample-data excluder** — test records in responses are sample data rather than real personal-data leaks.
12660. **Lorem-ipsum content filter** — placeholder content is excluded from information-disclosure analysis.
12661. **Staging-banner detector** — staging and development banners route findings to environment-qualified status.
12662. **Feature-flag evaluator** — disabled features endpoints are labeled dormant rather than vulnerable unless actually reachable.
12663. **Maintenance-page detector** — maintenance-mode responses are excluded from analysis entirely.
12664. **Coming-soon page excluder** — placeholder sites generate zero findings and only a no-attack-surface note.
12665. **Honeypot-behavior profiler** — profiles responses for honeypot tells such as instant fake vulnerabilities, tarpitting, and overly eager banners, quarantining the target when found.
12666. **Canary-token trip detector** — detects when probes hit canary tokens and immediately halts that vector to avoid burning the engagement.
12667. **Tarpit-timing detector** — identifies artificially slow responses designed to trap scanners, and timing evidence from tarpits is discarded.
12668. **Fake-vulnerability honeypot filter** — honeypots faking SQLi or XSS reflections are fingerprinted and their supposed findings suppressed.
12669. **Deception-port excluder** — ports that accept everything and emulate services are excluded from service-vulnerability analysis.
12670. **Honeypot-software fingerprint** — matches known honeypot software signatures before reporting service flaws.
12671. **Greylist-behavior detector** — identifies greylisting mail servers so email-injection findings are not fabricated from deferrals.
12672. **Honey-user detector** — accounts that always succeed authentication are flagged as deception rather than authorization bypass.
12673. **Synthetic-monitoring endpoint excluder** — excludes uptime-monitor endpoints from anomaly baselines.
12674. **Security-scanner artifact filter** — detects residues of other scanners in logs and pages to avoid double-attributing their noise.
12675. **Bounty-platform probe detector** — identifies platform-injected test traffic and excludes it from baselines.
12676. **Client-side honeypot detector** — detects JavaScript traps that fake DOM sinks for bots, and findings from trap code are suppressed.
12677. **Fake-admin-panel filter** — honeypot admin panels accepting any credentials are fingerprinted rather than reported as authentication bypass.
12678. **Active-monitoring disclaimer** — notes when target behaviors suggest active monitoring and adjusts probe aggressiveness accordingly.
12679. **Deception-consistency check** — verifies the target claimed stack matches its behavior, and mismatches trigger honeypot suspicion.
12680. **Response-too-perfect detector** — flags responses that look crafted for scanners such as instant textbook SQL errors as likely deception.
12681. **Impossible-service banner filter** — banners advertising impossible version combinations are treated as deception markers.
12682. **Honeypot-confidence score** — every target gets a honeypot-likelihood score, and high scores route all findings to manual review.
12683. **Deception-aware probe budget** — reduces probe aggressiveness automatically as honeypot likelihood rises.
12684. **Post-honeypot evidence purge** — when a target is later identified as a honeypot, all its findings are purged with an audit note.
12685. **Scope-deception guard** — verifies the target actually belongs to the authorized scope, and out-of-scope lookalikes are never probed.
12686. **Typosquat-target guard** — detects lookalike domains in scope lists and requires explicit confirmation before probing.
12687. **Parked-domain detector** — parked pages generate no findings.
12688. **Domain-for-sale detector** — sale landing pages are excluded from analysis.
12689. **Expired-domain guard** — expired domains are flagged rather than hunted.
12690. **CDN-placeholder detector** — default CDN landing pages are excluded.
12691. **Webhost-default-page filter** — default hosting pages generate no findings.
12692. **Wildcard-DNS trap detector** — detects wildcard DNS that makes every subdomain resolve, since takeover claims need real dangling records.
12693. **DNS-sinkhole detector** — identifies sinkholed domains and halts probing.
12694. **Environment-fingerprint confidence** — the environment classification itself is scored, and low-confidence classifications do not suppress findings.
12695. **Multi-tenant shared-IP attributor** — attributes findings to the correct virtual host on shared IPs so neighbor-tenant behaviors are not filed as the target vulnerabilities.
12696. **SNI-routing verifier** — verifies requests actually reached the intended virtual host through SNI and Host consistency rather than a default host.
12697. **Default-vhost response filter** — excludes default virtual-host responses from the target findings.
12698. **Reverse-proxy header audit** — documents which headers the proxy strips or adds so findings are not attributed to stripped protections.
12699. **Proxy-versus-origin behavior diff** — diffs proxied against direct responses to attribute behaviors correctly.
12700. **Geo-fenced behavior labeler** — labels findings that only reproduce from certain regions.
12701. **Time-fenced behavior detector** — identifies behaviors occurring only in specific windows such as maintenance or batch jobs and labels them.
12702. **A/B-test variant attributor** — attributes findings to the specific variant or bucket that produced them.
12703. **Blue-green deployment guard** — detects mid-hunt deploys through version flips and re-baselines instead of mixing evidence across versions.
12704. **Environment-fingerprint report appendix** — the PDF documents the full environment classification so clients can dispute it.
12705. **Root-cause merge key** — findings merge on root cause and sink location rather than on URL and payload, so one flaw yields exactly one finding.
12706. **Redirect-chain collapser** — findings on every hop of a redirect chain collapse into the originating flaw.
12707. **Parameter-variant merger** — the same flaw reached through different parameter names merges into one finding with all vectors listed.
12708. **Payload-canonicalizer** — normalizes payloads across encoding, case, and whitespace before deduplication so trivial variants do not multiply findings.
12709. **HTTP and HTTPS duplicate merger** — the same flaw on both schemes merges with both URLs noted.
12710. **WWW versus apex merger** — findings merge across www and apex variants when they serve the same application.
12711. **Trailing-slash normalizer** — path variants with and without trailing slashes merge when they hit the same handler.
12712. **Case-variant path merger** — paths differing only in case merge when the server treats them identically.
12713. **Session-specific dedup guard** — findings differing only by session identifier merge, and session identifiers are stripped from merge keys.
12714. **Timestamp-noise stripper** — timestamps, nonces, and request identifiers are stripped before similarity comparison.
12715. **Error-message template merger** — different user inputs producing the same error template merge into one input-validation finding.
12716. **Subdomain-service merger** — the same vulnerable service on ten subdomains becomes one finding with an affected-hosts list.
12717. **Port-variant merger** — the same flaw on multiple ports merges into one finding.
12718. **API-version merger** — the same flaw across API versions merges unless the versions genuinely differ in code.
12719. **Mobile-versus-web parity merger** — the same backend flaw reached through app and web merges with both vectors documented.
12720. **Language-locale merger** — findings reproduced across locales merge into one.
12721. **Encoding-variant merger** — UTF-8, UTF-16, and double-encoded variants of one flaw merge.
12722. **Method-variant merger** — GET and POST variants of the same injection merge.
12723. **Fragment-versus-query merger** — DOM sinks reachable through hash or query merge when the sink is identical.
12724. **Near-duplicate fuzzy hasher** — similarity hashing over normalized evidence merges findings above point nine similarity for human review.
12725. **Merge-audit trail** — every merge records which findings merged and why, and reviewers can reverse any merge.
12726. **Merge-confidence propagation** — merged findings take the maximum confidence with all evidence attached rather than averaging down.
12727. **Severity-of-merged take-max** — merged severity is the maximum of members with documented rationale.
12728. **Unmerge request handler** — reviewers can unmerge with one click, and unmerges train the merger.
12729. **Cross-hunt root-cause linker** — links the same root cause across hunts into a persistent flaw record.
12730. **Flaw-lifecycle tracker** — tracks each flaw from first seen through confirmed, reported, fixed, and verified across hunts.
12731. **Regression re-opener** — when a supposedly fixed flaw reappears, it reopens with full history rather than filing as new.
12732. **Duplicate-threshold tuner** — merge thresholds are tuned per program from reviewer unmerge rates.
12733. **Merge-explanation generator** — each merged finding explains in one line why its members constitute the same flaw.
12734. **Dedup-precision monitor** — samples merged pairs for reviewer validation, and precision below point nine five triggers retuning.
12735. **CVE-version matcher** — matches detected software versions against CVE feeds so already-known CVEs are labeled rather than rediscovered.
12736. **Vendor-advisory correlator** — correlates findings with vendor security advisories to avoid reporting patched known issues as new.
12737. **Patch-presence verifier** — verifies the patch is actually applied through behavioral testing rather than version claims.
12738. **Already-reported detector** — checks the program disclosed-report history where available to avoid duplicate submissions.
12739. **Public-disclosure search** — searches public writeups for the same flaw class on the target before reporting.
12740. **Changelog-miner** — mines changelogs and release notes for silent fixes matching the finding.
12741. **Fix-commit attributor** — links findings to upstream fix commits when the code is public.
12742. **NVD-description matcher** — fuzzy-matches finding descriptions against NVD entries for the detected stack.
12743. **Exploit-database correlation** — correlates with public exploits for the version, and known-exploit plus unpatched escalates rather than reports as new.
12744. **Dependency-advisory cross-check** — checks dependency findings against package advisories with reachability analysis.
12745. **Reachability-gated dependency reporting** — unreachable vulnerable functions are labeled rather than reported as exploitable.
12746. **Transitive-dependency attributor** — attributes the flaw to the correct dependency in the tree.
12747. **Backport-patch detector** — detects backported patches that keep version numbers static through behavioral tests before claiming CVE applicability.
12748. **Distro-patch tracker** — accounts for distribution-backported security fixes that keep version numbers unchanged.
12749. **EOL-software qualifier** — end-of-life software is a risk note, and specific vulnerabilities still need proof.
12750. **Known-FP-signature library** — maintains signatures of scanner-known false positives and pre-filters them.
12751. **Vendor-FP-list subscriber** — ingests vendors published false-positive lists for their own products.
12752. **Upstream-fix re-verification** — re-tests after upstream patches with the original proof of concept.
12753. **Disclosure-timeline checker** — verifies whether the issue is already past its disclosure deadline and therefore public knowledge.
12754. **Upstream-attribution labeler** — labels findings as known-upstream versus novel explicitly in the report.
12755. **Cross-hunt flapping detector** — findings that appear and disappear across hunts trigger a stability investigation rather than silent re-reporting.
12756. **Baseline-drift monitor** — tracks endpoint behavior baselines across hunts, since drift explains supposed new findings that are actually environmental.
12757. **Finding-persistence scorer** — scores findings by consecutive confirming hunts, and one-hunt wonders are labeled.
12758. **Inter-hunt evidence linker** — links evidence across hunts so reviewers see the complete history.
12759. **Hunt-comparability gate** — compares only hunts with similar scope and configuration, normalizing configuration changes first.
12760. **Target-evolution tracker** — records target changes in tech stack and WAF between hunts to explain confidence shifts.
12761. **Seasonal-behavior guard** — accounts for time-of-day and day-of-week behavior differences before declaring changes.
12762. **Config-drift explainer** — when a finding vanishes, checks for configuration or WAF changes before declaring it fixed.
12763. **Silent-fix detector** — detects fixes with no changelog through behavioral diffing across hunts.
12764. **Regression-window measurer** — measures how long a fix stayed fixed before regressing.
12765. **Hunt-quality scorer** — scores each hunt verification rigor, and low-rigor hunts findings are re-verified before reporting.
12766. **Cross-hunt reviewer-consistency** — tracks whether different reviewers decide similar findings similarly, and divergence triggers calibration.
12767. **Inter-hunt FP-pattern learner** — mines false positives recurring across hunts into the pattern library automatically.
12768. **Program-FP-rate tracker** — tracks false-positive rate per program over time, and rising rates trigger detector audits.
12769. **Detector-version attributor** — attributes false-positive-rate changes to detector version changes.
12770. **Hunt-parameter recorder** — records every hunt configuration so results are reproducible and comparable.
12771. **Reproducibility verifier** — re-runs a sample of old hunts confirmations to verify the pipeline still agrees with itself.
12772. **Longitudinal-confidence plot** — plots each persistent finding confidence over time in internal dashboards.
12773. **Stale-finding reaper** — findings unconfirmed for ninety days are archived rather than carried forward silently.
12774. **Inter-hunt consistency report** — produces an internal monthly quality report on flapping, drift, and persistence.
12775. **Per-endpoint response profiler** — profiles status, length, and timing distributions per endpoint from benign traffic before any attack probing.
12776. **Baseline-warmup requirement** — no anomaly-based finding is raised until the baseline holds at least fifty benign samples.
12777. **Delta-threshold per endpoint** — anomaly thresholds derive from the endpoint own variance rather than global constants.
12778. **Benign-parameter fuzzer** — learns normal parameter shapes such as numeric identifiers and enums to distinguish malformed-input errors from injection.
12779. **Normal-error catalog** — catalogs the endpoint normal error responses so ordinary errors are not mistaken for injection oracles.
12780. **Timing-baseline per endpoint** — each endpoint gets its own latency distribution, and global timing thresholds are banned.
12781. **Length-baseline per endpoint** — response-length anomalies are judged against the endpoint own history.
12782. **Status-code norm tracker** — learns which statuses are normal per endpoint since some APIs legitimately return 404 responses.
12783. **Redirect-norm mapper** — learns normal redirect patterns so open-redirect detection is not fooled by normal flows.
12784. **Content-type norm enforcer** — flags only deviations from the endpoint normal content types.
12785. **Authentication-norm profiler** — learns which endpoints normally require authentication, and missing-authentication claims are judged against the norm.
12786. **Rate-limit norm learner** — learns normal rate-limit behavior to avoid mistaking throttling for vulnerability signals.
12787. **Baseline-contamination guard** — ensures attack probes do not pollute the benign baseline by keeping traffic classes separate.
12788. **Baseline-refresh cadence** — baselines refresh weekly, and stale baselines are labeled.
12789. **Concept-drift detector** — detects when an endpoint behavior distribution shifts after a deploy and triggers re-baselining.
12790. **Cold-start caution** — new endpoints with thin baselines get wider uncertainty intervals.
12791. **Multi-modal baseline handler** — endpoints with legitimately multimodal behavior such as fast cache hits and slow misses model both modes.
12792. **Baseline-explainability** — reviewers can inspect the baseline samples behind any anomaly claim.
12793. **Adversarial-baseline-poisoning guard** — detects attempts to poison baselines through slow-drip anomalous traffic.
12794. **Baseline-sharing across similar endpoints** — pools baselines for endpoints with identical handlers together with similarity justification.
12795. **Read-only re-verification mode** — re-verification replays use only GET and HEAD plus provably non-mutating requests.
12796. **Canary-token re-proof** — every re-verification uses fresh unique canaries so old artifacts cannot validate new claims.
12797. **Non-mutating SQLi re-proof** — re-proves SQLi with SELECT-only payloads, and any write primitive is re-tested in read-only form.
12798. **Revert-verified write proofs** — any mutating proof must demonstrate the revert succeeded before the finding is filed.
12799. **Rate-limited re-verification** — re-probes run at no more than ten percent of the original probe rate to avoid disrupting the target.
12800. **Off-hours re-verification scheduler** — heavy re-verification runs during the target off-hours where timezone is known.
12801. **Scope re-check pre-probe** — re-verification re-confirms the target remains in authorized scope before sending any packet.
12802. **Data-minimization in evidence** — stored evidence contains canaries and metadata but never real user data.
12803. **PII-scrubber for evidence** — automated scrubbing removes PII-shaped strings from all stored probe evidence.
12804. **Safe-mode attestation** — the report attests which proofs were non-destructive and which required mutation with authorization.
12805. **Expected-value queue ordering** — orders reviews by impact times confidence times novelty rather than arrival time.
12806. **Review-budget allocator** — distributes reviewer attention by expected value, so low-value findings get sampled rather than fully reviewed.
12807. **One-click confirm and dismiss** — reviewers decide in a single click because friction is the enemy of throughput.
12808. **Reason-capture on dismiss** — dismissals require a reason from the taxonomy, and reasonless dismissals are rejected by the interface.
12809. **Reason-capture on confirm** — confirmations record which evidence convinced the reviewer, training the system on success patterns.
12810. **Top-five daily digest** — reviewers receive the five highest-value unconfirmed findings daily rather than a firehose.
12811. **SLA-per-severity timer** — Critical reviews are due in four hours and High in twenty-four, with breaches escalating automatically.
12812. **Stale-review reaper** — reviews idle past SLA are reassigned rather than left to rot.
12813. **Review-context bundle** — each review shows evidence, baselines, similar past decisions, and the confidence math in one view.
12814. **Side-by-side evidence viewer** — shows probe versus control responses side by side for fast differential judgment.
12815. **Confidence-sorted batches** — reviewers work batches sorted by confidence so calibration stays anchored.
12816. **Blind-review mode** — hides the agent severity and confidence on a sample to measure reviewer independence.
12817. **Review-fatigue monitor** — tracks decisions per hour, and fatigued reviewers are routed low-stakes items.
12818. **Queue-health dashboard** — shows queue depth, age distribution, and false-positive rate in real time.
12819. **Auto-escalation on disagreement** — agent-high-confidence plus reviewer-dismiss triggers a second reviewer automatically.
12820. **Dismissal-appeal path** — the agent can appeal dismissals with new evidence, and appeals are tracked.
12821. **Reviewer-workload balancer** — distributes load evenly because overloaded reviewers make worse decisions.
12822. **Mobile-review triage** — critical findings are reviewable from a phone with the full evidence bundle.
12823. **Review-deadline negotiator** — reviewers can request evidence top-ups instead of deciding blind.
12824. **Queue-priority override audit** — manual priority overrides are logged with reasons.
12825. **Reviewer-reputation scorer** — tracks each reviewer precision and recall against ground truth, and reputation weights future votes.
12826. **New-reviewer probation** — new reviewers decisions are shadow-scored against seniors for fifty cases before counting fully.
12827. **Reviewer-calibration sessions** — monthly blind sets with known answers keep reviewers honest.
12828. **Inter-reviewer agreement tracker** — tracks agreement coefficients per finding class, and low-agreement classes get rubric rewrites.
12829. **Consensus-threshold rule** — Critical findings need two independent confirmations and High needs one, with no single-reviewer Criticals allowed.
12830. **Independent-second-review** — the second reviewer sees raw evidence rather than the first reviewer verdict.
12831. **Disagreement-resolution protocol** — tied reviews go to a senior arbiter with both rationales preserved.
12832. **Dissent-preservation rule** — minority opinions stay attached to the finding permanently.
12833. **Reviewer-bias detector** — detects reviewers who always confirm or always dismiss and recalibrates their weight.
12834. **Automation-bias guard** — reviewers must open the evidence bundle before the confirm button enables, blocking blind trust in the agent.
12835. **Seniority-weighted voting** — votes weight by reputation rather than title, so a sharp junior can outvote a careless senior.
12836. **Blind re-review sampler** — five percent of decided findings get a blind second review to measure decision quality.
12837. **Review-decision audit log** — every decision records who decided, when, which evidence version, and why.
12838. **Decision-reversal tracker** — tracks reversals, and high-reversal reviewers get coaching rather than punishment.
12839. **Reviewer-feedback latency** — measures time from review to agent-behavior change, and slow loops are escalated.
12840. **Expertise-router** — routes cryptography findings to cryptography reviewers and web findings to web reviewers, with mismatched routing measured and fixed.
12841. **Reviewer-confidence elicitation** — reviewers record their own confidence, and agent-versus-human confidence gaps are analyzed.
12842. **Abstention option** — reviewers can abstain with a reason, since forced decisions on unclear evidence produce noise.
12843. **Abstention-routing** — abstained findings route to specialists or automatically gather more evidence.
12844. **Review-quality scorecard** — produces a monthly per-reviewer quality report that stays private and coaching oriented.
12845. **Dismissal-reason to detector patch** — every dismissal reason maps to a detector-improvement ticket, and the loop is tracked to closure.
12846. **FP-pattern auto-miner** — clusters dismissal reasons into new false-positive-pattern library entries automatically.
12847. **Confirm-pattern reinforcer** — confirmed findings evidence patterns strengthen the corresponding detectors.
12848. **Reviewer-note NLP miner** — mines free-text reviewer notes for recurring false-positive themes.
12849. **Threshold auto-tuner** — dismissal rates per class automatically nudge promotion thresholds weekly.
12850. **Probe-technique deprecator** — techniques with sustained low precision are auto-deprecated with a migration note.
12851. **Detector-changelog per finding** — findings show which detector version found them so feedback lands on the right code.
