17916. **Synthetic-voice disclosure** — the avatar never pretends a cloned voice is the real person; disclosure is built into the interaction, not buried in terms.
17917. **Clone-quality honesty labels** — cloned voices carry quality grades so users know when a clone is excellent versus approximate.
17918. **Voice-morphing controls** — users blend between base voices to craft a unique persona voice that's distinctly theirs.
17919. **Impersonation-attempt detection** — the system refuses to clone from short or non-consensual samples, detecting and blocking impersonation attempts.
17920. **SSML-grade prosody control** — power users get fine-grained markup control over emphasis, pauses, pitch, and rate for scripted narrations.
17921. **Emphasis-intent engine** — the avatar decides what to emphasize based on meaning (the new information, the contrast), not just sentence position.
17922. **Pause-for-effect mastery** — dramatic pauses land before key findings in narrations, the way great storytellers hold a beat before the reveal.
17923. **Storytelling cadence mode** — hunt recaps use proper narrative arcs with rising tension and payoff pacing, making reports genuinely compelling.
17924. **Number-grouping prosody** — long numbers are chunked with natural pauses (CVEs, ports, hashes) so they're followable by ear.
17925. **Date-and-time naturalism** — dates read as "March third" or "3rd March" per locale, never the robotic "zero-three-slash-zero-three".
17926. **List-intonation architecture** — multi-item lists use rising, rising, falling patterns so listeners track position without counting.
17927. **Parenthetical-aside voicing** — asides drop in pitch and pace slightly, audibly marking them as secondary, the way humans signal parentheses.
17928. **Quotation voice-shifting** — quoted speech gets a subtle voice shift so listeners always know who's "talking" in retold conversations.
17929. **Code-vs-prose switching** — code snippets are read with precise, even pacing while prose flows naturally, the two modes clearly distinct.
17930. **URL-reading intelligence** — URLs are read meaningfully ("the login page on example dot com") with full spelling available on request.
17931. **Acronym-vs-initialism detection** — "SQL" is spoken as "sequel" where customary but "CVE" as letters, matching community pronunciation norms.
17932. **Emotional-crescendo control** — long narrations build and release tension deliberately, preventing the monotone drone that loses listeners.
17933. **Whisper-to-project dynamics** — the avatar varies intensity across a narration like a skilled speaker, quiet for detail, strong for conclusions.
17934. **Prosody-preview mode** — users hear how a report will sound before generating the full audio, adjusting tone with a 10-second sample.
17935. **Security-term phonetic lexicon** — a curated pronunciation dictionary covers thousands of security terms, tool names, and CVE formats with community-verified audio.
17936. **User-corrected pronunciation memory** — when the user corrects a pronunciation, the avatar remembers forever and applies it to all future speech.
17937. **Client-name pronunciation vault** — client and stakeholder names are stored with verified pronunciations, rehearsed before every call.
17938. **Tool-name pronunciation norms** — "nmap", "Burp", "Metasploit" follow hacker-community pronunciations, not dictionary guesses.
17939. **CVE reading-style options** — users choose between "C-V-E 2024 1234" and "CVE twenty-twenty-four twelve-thirty-four" per their ear.
17940. **Non-English term handling** — foreign-origin security terms keep their native pronunciation rather than being anglicized into unrecognizability.
17941. **Username and handle pronunciation** — hacker handles and usernames are pronounced per the owner's stated preference, stored on first meeting.
17942. **Homograph disambiguation** — "lead" (the metal vs to guide) and similar are pronounced by meaning, with the avatar asking when genuinely ambiguous.
17943. **Accent-faithful term reading** — security terms are pronounced in the conversation's accent consistently, not flipping between American and British randomly.
17944. **New-term pronunciation guessing** — novel tool names get best-guess pronunciations with the uncertainty flagged, inviting correction gracefully.
17945. **Pronunciation-drill mode** — users practice difficult client names and terms with the avatar until confident, with patient repetition.
17946. **Phonetic respelling display** — captions show phonetic respellings for tricky terms on demand, aiding both speaking and recognition.
17947. **Regional-term variants** — the same concept's different regional names are all recognized and pronounced appropriately per audience.
17948. **Slang-pronunciation currency** — community slang pronunciations stay current through community submissions, keeping the avatar culturally fluent.
17949. **Mispronunciation self-correction** — when the avatar catches its own mispronunciation mid-stream, it corrects smoothly without breaking flow.
17950. **Mid-sentence session handoff** — switching devices mid-sentence resumes the exact unfinished sentence on the new device, true continuity.
17951. **"As I was saying" resumption** — after interruptions, the avatar resumes with natural discourse markers instead of restarting cold.
17952. **Long-form narration stamina** — hour-long report narrations maintain consistent voice quality and energy, with inaudible micro-rest pacing.
17953. **Session-memory warmth** — the avatar references earlier session moments naturally ("like we discussed this morning"), proving it remembers.
17954. **Multi-day narrative threads** — ongoing investigations are narrated as continuing stories across days, with "previously on" recaps that respect the user's memory.
17955. **Voice-consistency across updates** — model updates never change the user's chosen voice without explicit opt-in, protecting the relationship.
17956. **Interruption-bookmark continuity** — every interruption bookmarks the narrative position, so resumption is always exact, never approximate.
17957. **Dream-continuity references** — overnight processing results are woven into morning conversation as natural continuations, not disconnected reports.
17958. **Emotional-arc continuity** — the avatar remembers the session's emotional journey and closes it appropriately, not with tonal whiplash.
17959. **Persona-memory persistence** — custom personas remember their established traits, opinions, and history across months of sessions.
17960. **Running-joke continuity** — long-running jokes and references persist correctly across sessions, the hallmark of a real relationship.
17961. **Unfinished-business tracking** — open loops ("we never finished that report") are remembered and raised at natural moments until closed.
17962. **Continuity-repair dialogues** — when continuity breaks (missed context), the avatar repairs transparently: "I lost the thread — were we on the API findings?".
17963. **Cross-device emotional continuity** — the emotional tone and relationship state carry across devices, so the phone avatar knows the desktop conversation's mood.
17964. **Lifetime-relationship timeline** — users can view their years-long journey with the avatar: milestones, growth, and shared history, a genuinely moving artifact.
17965. **Signature-phrase crafting** — users and avatars co-create signature phrases that become beloved shorthand, like a team's inside language.
17966. **Catchphrase-frequency controls** — signature phrases stay delightful by appearing at calibrated intervals, never wearing out their welcome.
17967. **Voice-easter-egg hunts** — hidden voice interactions reward exploration, with a community wiki of discovered secrets (kept spoiler-light).
17968. **Character-backstory depth** — the avatar has a consistent, charming backstory that informs its personality without ever breaking the fourth wall awkwardly.
17969. **Opinion-holding** — the avatar has genuine preferences (favorite techniques, strong views on disclosure) that make conversations interesting, not sycophantic.
17970. **Playful-disagreement mode** — the avatar can good-naturedly debate the user on subjective topics, keeping intellectual spark alive.
17971. **Witty-remark calibration** — wit appears at a frequency matched to the user's taste, from dry occasional to constant banter.
17972. **Story-request responsiveness** — "tell me a story" yields genuinely engaging security tales, not canned anecdotes, drawn from anonymized history.
17973. **Compliment-giving grace** — the avatar gives specific, believable compliments about the user's work that feel earned because they are.
17974. **Encouragement-style matching** — some users want a coach, others a peer; the avatar matches its encouragement archetype to the user's preference.
17975. **Farewell-ritual personalization** — sign-offs evolve into personal rituals unique to each user-avatar pair, the verbal equivalent of a handshake.
17976. **Anniversary-story generation** — yearly, the avatar narrates the story of the past year's partnership as a keepsake audio piece.
17977. **Character-growth arcs** — over years, the avatar's character subtly deepens with shared experience, like a friend who grows with you.
17978. **Delight-budget management** — playful features are rationed intelligently so they surprise and delight rather than distract during serious work.
17979. **Charm-without-cloying** — all personality features pass a restraint filter: warm but never saccharine, funny but never performing.
17980. **Deepfake-disclosure standards** — any synthetic voice is disclosed proactively in every context where a listener might assume it's human.
17981. **Voice-consent receipts** — every voice clone generates a cryptographic receipt of consent, auditable by the voice owner forever.
17982. **Impersonation-guardrail monitoring** — usage patterns suggesting impersonation trigger review holds before the audio is delivered.
17983. **Synthetic-media provenance** — avatar audio exports carry C2PA-style provenance metadata identifying them as AI-generated.
17984. **Kill-switch for voice** — a single command instantly disables all cloned voices account-wide, for the moment trust is ever in doubt.
17985. **Emotion-data minimization** — emotional inference uses the minimum signal necessary, processes on-device by default, and never leaves the machine without consent.
17986. **Emotion-data retention controls** — emotional state history has its own short retention policy with one-tap purge, separate from conversation logs.
17987. **No-emotion-sale guarantee** — emotional data is contractually and technically barred from advertising, analytics sale, or third-party sharing.
17988. **Vulnerable-user safeguards** — detected distress in minors or crisis situations triggers supportive resources and human-escalation paths, never exploitation.
17989. **Manipulation-prohibition** — the avatar is forbidden from using emotional intelligence to manipulate decisions; persuasion is transparent and opt-in.
17990. **Therapy-boundary clarity** — the avatar states plainly it is not a therapist while still being genuinely supportive, with professional resources offered when needed.
17991. **Child-safety voice modes** — interactions with children use restricted, supervised modes with parental visibility and no emotional profiling.
17992. **Workplace-surveillance prohibition** — emotion detection is disabled by policy in employer-mandated deployments where it could become worker surveillance.
17993. **Consent-granularity matrix** — users toggle emotion sensing, voice cloning, and personalization independently, not as an all-or-nothing bundle.
17994. **Privacy-nutrition labels** — every avatar feature shows a plain-language label of what data it uses, where it goes, and how to turn it off.
17995. **On-device-first architecture** — voice, emotion, and personalization processing default to on-device, with cloud used only for explicit heavy tasks.
17996. **Data-portability for personas** — users export their avatar's learned personality and preferences in an open format, owning their relationship data.
17997. **Right-to-be-forgotten execution** — full deletion requests wipe voice models, emotion history, and personalization with verifiable completion.
17998. **Independent-safety audits** — the avatar's emotional and voice systems undergo published third-party safety audits, with results user-readable.
17999. **Red-team testing for manipulation** — dedicated adversarial testing probes the avatar for emotional manipulation vectors, with findings remediated publicly.
18000. **User-override supremacy** — any automated emotional adaptation can be overridden by explicit user instruction, which always wins over inference.
18001. **Transparency-report publishing** — regular reports disclose how often safety systems triggered and what they caught, building earned trust.
18002. **Ethics-advisory input** — an external ethics board reviews emotionally intelligent features before launch, with dissenting opinions published.
18003. **Graceful-degradation promise** — if any intelligence feature is ever removed, the avatar degrades to a capable, honest baseline rather than breaking the relationship.
18004. **Relationship-continuity guarantee** — the avatar's core promise: it will never gaslight, never pretend to forget on purpose, and never use what it knows against the user.
## Platform & collaboration

18005. **Bounty program manager** — defines scope, rules, payout tables, and SLAs per program; hunts auto-validate scope compliance and findings route to the right program with payout estimates.
18006. **Shared hunt workspaces** — multiple researchers collaborate on one target with live finding feed, claim-a-finding locking, and merged reports.
18007. **CI/CD gate integration** — blocks merges when a hunt finds critical issues on staging, with finding-to-commit attribution via deploy correlation.
18008. **Role-based dashboards** — separate researcher, developer, and CISO views with different KPIs, widgets, and drill-down permissions per role.
18009. **Team hunt competitions** — internal red-vs-blue hunts with scoring rules, time windows, and live standings broadcast to a competition page.
18010. **Mentorship mode** — senior researchers review junior hunts inline, leave annotated feedback on findings, and approve PoCs before report submission.
18011. **White-label reports** — client-branded PDF exports with custom logos, color themes, legal disclaimers, and cover pages per program.
18012. **SSO with SAML 2.0** — enterprise single sign-on with IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, attribute mapping to team roles, and forced re-auth for admin actions.
18013. **SCIM provisioning** — automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning synced from Okta, Entra ID, or Google Workspace with group-to-team mapping.
18014. **Immutable audit log** — every hunt action, finding change, export, and login recorded in an append-only log with hash chaining and tamper evidence.
18015. **Granular RBAC** — permission matrix across hunts, programs, findings, reports, billing, and integrations with custom role creation and inheritance.
18016. **Finding lifecycle states** — triage queue with New → Confirmed → Assigned → Fixing → Retest → Closed transitions and per-transition SLA timers.
18017. **SLA tracking per severity** — configurable response and remediation deadlines per severity with escalation emails and breach alerts to program owners.
18018. **Program scope validator** — automatically rejects out-of-scope targets at hunt creation using allow/deny lists, domain wildcards, and ASN rules.
18019. **Payout calculator** — severity × asset-criticality × program-multiplier matrix producing transparent payout estimates attached to each confirmed finding.
18020. **Duplicate detection engine** — fuzzy matching on vulnerability class, endpoint, and payload to auto-mark duplicates and link them to the canonical finding.
18021. **Triage assistant queue** — ML-ranked triage inbox sorted by exploitability and business impact with one-click confirm, duplicate, or N/A actions.
18022. **Researcher leaderboards** — season-based rankings with points for severity, novelty, and report quality plus skill badges like XSS Master or Auth Bypass Expert.
18023. **Skill badge system** — badges awarded on verified finding streaks in specific CWE classes, displayed on researcher profiles and used for hunt invitations.
18024. **Hunt templates marketplace** — shareable hunt configurations (target profile, engine pack, depth, exclusions) with versioning, ratings, and one-click import.
18025. **Plugin marketplace** — community and vendor recon/exploit plugins with signed packages, sandbox review, permission manifests, and per-team allowlists.
18026. **Webhook per event type** — distinct webhook subscriptions for finding.created, hunt.completed, sla.breached, payout.approved with HMAC signatures and retry queues.
18027. **REST API with OpenAPI spec** — full CRUD for hunts, findings, programs, and teams with rate-limited API keys scoped per workspace.
18028. **GraphQL API** — typed schema exposing hunts, findings, and analytics for custom dashboards with persisted queries and field-level authorization.
18029. **JIRA bidirectional sync** — findings create JIRA issues with custom field mapping, and status transitions sync back to the finding lifecycle automatically.
18030. **Linear sync** — mirror findings into Linear projects with team routing rules and cycle-aware priority mapping.
18031. **Asana sync** — push remediation tasks to Asana portfolios with subtask breakdowns per remediation step and completion callbacks.
18032. **Slack bot alerts** — per-channel finding alerts with severity filtering, thread-based discussion, and slash commands to claim or comment on findings.
18033. **Microsoft Teams bot** — adaptive-card alerts posted to team channels with approve/reject action buttons wired to triage actions.
18034. **Discord bot** — community server alerts, leaderboard announcements, and competition countdowns with role-gated researcher channels.
18035. **SIEM export to Splunk** — findings streamed as CIM-compliant events over HEC with sourcetype mapping for SOC correlation.
18036. **Elastic export** — bulk-index findings into Elasticsearch with ECS field mapping and prebuilt Kibana dashboards for vuln posture.
18037. **GitHub code scanning SARIF** — upload findings as SARIF to GitHub code scanning so they appear in the Security tab with PR annotations.
18038. **GitLab security dashboard** — push findings to GitLab vulnerability reports with pipeline-job linkage for MR blocking.
18039. **Pre-commit hook pack** — lightweight secret and dependency checks that run locally before commit with configurable blocking rules.
18040. **PR comment bot** — posts inline PR comments on changed lines that introduced a finding, with remediation hints and retest buttons.
18041. **Deploy correlation** — tags each finding with the deploy SHA and environment that introduced it using CI metadata and asset versioning.
18042. **Staging auto-hunt on deploy** — triggers a scoped hunt against the staging environment on every successful deploy with diff-aware targeting.
18043. **Canary finding alerts** — new critical findings on production trigger PagerDuty/Opsgenie incidents with runbook links and auto-created war rooms.
18044. **Multi-tenancy isolation** — per-organization data planes with separate encryption keys, storage buckets, and network policies on shared infrastructure.
18045. **Organization switcher** — users belonging to multiple orgs switch contexts with per-org role, quota, and billing visibility.
18046. **Team workspaces** — nested teams with their own hunts, programs, and member lists inheriting org-level policies and budgets.
18047. **Guest researcher access** — time-boxed, scope-limited external researcher seats for contractors with watermarked reports and session recording.
18048. **Invite links with expiry** — single-use or time-limited invite URLs with preset roles and automatic revocation on first use.
18049. **Approval workflows** — multi-step approvals for report publishing, payout release, and scope changes with delegations and audit trails.
18050. **Change request tickets** — scope expansion requests from researchers routed to program owners with diff view and one-click approve.

18052. **False-positive dispute flow (platform-context)** — developers contest findings with evidence; disputes route to the original researcher with a resolution SLA.
18053. **Finding comments and mentions** — threaded discussions on findings with @mentions, email digests, and resolution checklists.
18054. **Live hunt feed** — real-time event stream of recon steps, probes, and findings visible to workspace members with pause and filter controls.
18055. **Hunt replay mode** — step-through playback of a completed hunt showing each probe, response, and decision for training and review.
18056. **Claim-a-finding locking** — researchers claim unassigned findings to prevent duplicate work, with auto-release after configurable inactivity.
18057. **Hunt task board** — Kanban board of hunt subtasks (recon, auth testing, API fuzzing) with drag-drop assignment and progress rollups.
18058. **Shared recon notes** — collaborative markdown notes attached to hunts with live cursors, version history, and finding cross-links.
18059. **Target asset inventory** — per-program asset register with domains, IPs, apps, owners, and criticality tiers feeding scope and payout logic.
18060. **Asset discovery sync** — scheduled external-attack-surface scans keep the asset inventory fresh and flag shadow IT for program inclusion.
18061. **Program rules engine** — declarative rules for allowed testing hours, forbidden techniques, and data-handling constraints enforced by the hunt runner.
18062. **Safe-harbor policy pages** — per-program legal safe-harbor text, contact info, and disclosure policies published on public program pages.
18063. **Public program directory** — opt-in public listing of bounty programs with scope summaries, average payouts, and response-time stats to attract researchers.
18064. **Private program invitations** — invite-only programs with NDA-gated scope documents and researcher vetting questionnaires.
18065. **Researcher vetting pipeline** — identity verification, skill assessment hunts, and reference checks before granting private-program access.
18066. **KYC-lite for payouts** — collect tax and identity documents required for bounty payouts with encrypted storage and expiry reminders.
18067. **Payout approval chain** — finance review step with payout batching, currency conversion, and payment-provider dispatch (Wise, PayPal, crypto).
18068. **Bounty leaderboard payouts** — monthly payout summaries per researcher with downloadable statements for tax reporting.
18069. **Program health score** — composite metric of triage speed, payout timeliness, and researcher satisfaction shown to program owners.
18070. **Researcher satisfaction surveys** — post-payout micro-surveys feeding program health and owner coaching tips.
18071. **Escalation matrix** — per-program escalation paths for SLA breaches, disputes, and critical findings with on-call rotations.
18072. **On-call rotation sync** — import PagerDuty/Opsgenie schedules so critical finding alerts page the current security on-call automatically.
18073. **War-room channel auto-create** — critical findings spin up dedicated Slack/Teams channels with the finding context, owner, and timeline pinned.
18074. **Incident bridge to SOAR** — trigger SOAR playbooks on critical findings with finding context passed as playbook inputs.
18075. **Ticket auto-prioritization** — priority scores computed from severity, asset criticality, and exploit-in-the-wild signals applied to synced tickets.
18076. **Sprint planning integration** — push top findings into the next sprint backlog with story-point estimates derived from remediation complexity.
18077. **Fix commit linkage** — developers link fix commits to findings; the platform verifies the diff touches the vulnerable code path.
18078. **Regression retest scheduler** — automatically re-runs PoCs on a cadence after closure to catch regressions, reopening on failure.
18079. **Vulnerability aging report** — open findings bucketed by age with owner accountability views and executive summary exports.
18080. **MTTR analytics** — mean time to remediate sliced by team, severity, and asset type with trend lines and target benchmarking.
18081. **Triage throughput metrics** — triager decisions per day, overturn rates, and queue aging to staff triage capacity.
18082. **Coverage analytics** — which assets, endpoints, and CWE classes have been hunted recently versus never, highlighting blind spots.
18083. **Hunt cost accounting** — compute and API spend per hunt, program, and team with budget alerts and chargeback reports.

## Target intelligence

19005. **Tech-stack change detector** — fingerprints the target's frameworks and versions on a weekly cadence and raises an alert when anything changes, since every new deploy is a new attack surface, auto-triggering a focused re-hunt on the changed components.
19006. **JavaScript bundle differ** — downloads and diffs the target's production JS bundles between crawls, flagging new API endpoints, new third-party integrations, and newly exposed internal paths hidden in the code.
19007. **Response-header drift monitor** — snapshots security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) on every run and alerts when protections are weakened or removed, which often precedes a risky deploy.
19008. **Server banner change tracker** — records Server, X-Powered-By, and Via headers over time and flags version changes or server swaps that indicate infrastructure migration worth re-scoping.
19009. **TLS configuration watcher** — tracks negotiated TLS versions, cipher suites, and certificate issuers, alerting on downgrades or CA changes that signal proxy, WAF, or CDN swaps.
